newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel provident fund redemptions soar in August.
newsitem.headline: Israel provident fund redemptions soar in August.

text.p: Net public redemptions from Israel's provident funds in August soared to 2.241 billion shekels against redemptions of 943 million shekels in July, the Treasury said on Monday.
Since the beginning of the year net redemptions from provident funds totalled 7.376 billion shekels.
In August last year net redemptions from provident funds totalled 283.2 million shekels.
The Treasury said most of the money withdrawn from the provident funds was redeposited into shorter-term savings deposits.
Treasury figures reported that in August net deposits in savings plans totalled 1.475 billion shekels, against deposits of 832 million shekels in July.
Since the beginning of the year net deposits in savings plans totalled 3.232 billion shekels.

Provident funds are long-term savings funds with special tax benefits. Because of their poor performance, caused mainly by a falling stock market, the public has been withdrawing its money from the funds and investing in fixed-income savings plans.
